div.head: III Atr 2
div.ab: And þæt, þæt man cyðe mid gewitnesse, þæt nan man þæt ne awende æt cwícon þe ma þe æt déadon.
Et hoc quod per legitimum testimonium monstrabitur, nemo peruertat de uiuo plus quam de mortuo.
And þæt þæt man cyðe mid gewitnesse, þæt nan man þæt ne awende æt cwícon þe ma þe æt déadon.
Und was unter Zeugenschaft ausgesagt wird, dass niemand das umwerfen könne bei lebenden [Zeugen], so wenig wie [wenn sie] verstorben.
And what is declared with witness, that no one may overturn it in the case of living [witnesses] any more than of dead ones.
Secondly, declarations made with the support of witnesses shall be incontrovertible, whether the persons concerned be alive or dead.
And no man is to pervert what is declared with witness, no more when the persons are still alive than when they are dead.

note.seg: Schmid denkt an die amtlichen Zeugen (s. d. Gl 9a II. 13), wohl zu eng.—Für meine ursprüngliche Übersetzung ist es eine Parallele, wenn die Zeugen von Ælfreds Testament Pfand geben, þæt be hyra life hit nænig mann onwende; a. 880/85 Bi 553. Doch verstand Q, wie ich II 757 berichtigte: ‘bei lebendem [Zeugenführer, im Prozess Beweisenden], so wenig wie wenn er verstorben’.—Es kann hier nicht auch Eideshilfe verstanden sein, laut 2, 1.—Dauernde Rechtskraft rechtsförmlicher Akte wird wiederholt in 3

Schmid thinks of the official witnesses (see that word in Gl 9a II. 13), probably too narrowly.—A parallel to my original translation is the witnesses of Ælfred’s will giving pledge þæt be hyra life hit nænig mann onwende; a. 880/85 Bi 553. Q, however, understood it, as I corrected in II 757: ‘while [the leader of the witnesses, the party giving proof in the suit] is living, no more than if he had died’.—Oath-helping cannot also be meant here, according to 2, 1.—The lasting legal force of formal legal acts is repeated in 3

i.e. the persons who make declarations supported by witnesses. Liebermann in his translation takes cwicon, deadon as referring to the witnesses but corrects as above (Zeugenführer) in the Addenda to his first volume (see ii. p. 757) and in his notes (see iii. p. 157) in view of Q’s translation: Et hoc quod per legitimum testimonium monstrabitur, nemo pervertat de vivo plus quam de mortuo.

note.label: persons
note.seg: The Old English phrase is obscure: “with regard to the living no more than to the dead”. Liebermann at first took it to apply to the witnesses, later to the parties.
